issues.title: Pool-level USE failure leaves pooled connections on the old keyspace while pool believes otherwise
issues.verdictReason: PoolRefiller::use_keyspace (connection_pool.rs:1282-1325) sets self.current_keyspace optimistically before issuing any USE and never rolls it back or evicts a connection whose USE failed; Session::use_keyspace (session.rs:2007) and ClusterWorker (worker.rs:351) store it the same way. Already-pooled connections therefore keep serving the previous keyspace while the pool reports the new one, so unqualified statements silently hit the wrong keyspace.
issues.scopeReason: The optimistic store and the missing per-connection retry predate the diff; the PR only closes this for newly opened connections.

reportedAs.tob-diff-review: current_keyspace is stored optimistically and never rolled back (also at worker.rs:351, connection_pool.rs:1287).

issues.title: Permanently failing USE now drains every pool to Broken with no recovery path
issues.verdictReason: current_keyspace is set unconditionally in use_keyspace (connection_pool.rs:1287) and never cleared, and the new Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace) arm (connection_pool.rs:900-909) discards every connection whose USE fails. If the keyspace becomes permanently inaccessible, no connection can ever enter the pool: the pool empties, publishes MaybePoolConnections::Broken, and emit_events (connection_pool.rs:1158-1190) fires ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost for every node, so even fully-qualified queries fail. Pre-PR the connection stayed usable and only a warning was logged.
issues.scopeReason: The discard-on-USE-failure arm added by this PR is what converts a degraded-but-usable session into a fully-down cluster.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: PoolRefiller::use_keyspace sets current_keyspace unconditionally and never clears it on a failed USE, so every newly opened connection is now discarded and the pool loops in Broken/backoff forever, whereas before a failed USE on a fresh connection was just logged and the connection stayed usable.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: PoolRefiller::use_keyspace sets current_keyspace unconditionally before USE is attempted, and with discard-on-failure every new connection is rejected as long as USE keeps failing, draining pools, publishing Broken(UseKeyspaceError), and killing the session for all queries including fully-qualified ones; pre-PR this degraded gracefully, and the larger blast radius is undocumented.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: UseKeyspaceError includes permanently-failing variants; if the keyspace later becomes inaccessible, every new connection is discarded, the pool never fills, the node is reported down cluster-wide via ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost, and reconnect backoff grows unboundedly - a larger blast radius than 'preserves the current pool' suggests, worth a deliberate retryable-vs-permanent distinction.
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: post-PR every new connection with a failed use_keyspace is discarded, so pools never fill, the refiller churns full handshakes against every node forever at max_fill_backoff, and pools drain to Broken causing nodes to drop out of load balancing.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: A permanent USE KEYSPACE failure now prevents the pool from filling and publishes MaybePoolConnections::Broken (node reads as unreachable) instead of previously publishing a connection with the wrong keyspace; this user-visible trade-off is not called out anywhere discoverable in the PR.

issues.title: Untimed use_keyspace await in start_setting_keyspace_for_connection can wedge the refiller forever
issues.verdictReason: connection_pool.rs:1336 still carries '// TODO: There should be a timeout for this' and the await at 1341-1345 is unwrapped, unlike PoolRefiller::use_keyspace which wraps its USE in tokio::time::timeout(connect_timeout, ...) at 1310. A node that completes the handshake but never answers USE leaves the future pending in ready_connections, so is_filling() (connection_pool.rs:743) stays true and need_filling() never becomes true again.
issues.scopeReason: The untimed await and its TODO are byte-identical in semantics to main; the PR changed only what the future resolves to, not whether it can hang.

reportedAs.tob-rust-review: This await has no timeout (unlike the sibling PoolRefiller::use_keyspace, which wraps its USE in tokio::time::timeout), so a server that accepts the connection but never answers USE leaves the future pending forever, permanently stopping all refills for that node; the PR adds an explicit-failure path but doesn't close this silent-stall path.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: The `connection.use_keyspace(&keyspace_name).await` call has no timeout, so a node that accepts TCP but never answers USE leaves the future pending inside ready_connections forever, keeping is_filling() true indefinitely and preventing any further refill from being scheduled.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: The missing USE timeout at :1336 is a pre-existing TODO set aside as pre-existing/unrelated, though this PR enlarges its blast radius.

issues.title: Shard-aware-miss discard drops a counted connection without decrementing total_connections
issues.verdictReason: In the `else if evt.requested_shard.is_some()` arm (connection_pool.rs:994-1006) the owned Connection is dropped and replaced via start_opening_connection(None) with no dec_total_connections(); count_in_metrics already incremented it at open (connection_pool.rs:1046-1053) and nothing else decrements (grep shows the only dec sites are in connection_pool.rs). I added a probe test driving one accepted connection plus one shard-aware attempt onto the full shard: get_total_connections() read 2 with a single pooled connection.
issues.scopeReason: Commit de164845 explicitly sets out to balance total_connections across pool-discard sites and fixes three of four; this is the one it missed.

reportedAs.builtin-code-review: This branch drops an already-inc_total_connections()-counted Connection and retries on the regular port, leaving the one remaining hole in the decrement invariant the PR establishes elsewhere; under source-port-rewriting NAT the counter inflates without bound.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: In handle_ready_connection's shard-aware-port-miss branch, the connection is dropped without being stored anywhere, but inc_total_connections() was already called when it opened, so total_connections leaks upward on every shard-aware-port miss (e.g. behind NAT).
reportedAs.superpowers-review: A shard-aware connection landing on an already-full shard is dropped after inc_total_connections() charged it at :1051, with nothing decrementing it; reviewer reproduced the gauge drifting to 2 while the pool holds 1.
reportedAs.tob-rust-review: In the else-if arm for a requested shard, the owned connection is dropped without decrementing total_connections even though it was counted at open, permanently inflating the metric on every shard-aware connection landing on a full bucket.
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: The metrics-balancing commit fixes three of four discard sites, but the shard-mismatch drop at connection_pool.rs:994 still leaks.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: In the else if evt.requested_shard.is_some() branch (:994-1006), the excess shard-aware connection is dropped with no dec_total_connections() call, so the counter only ever drifts upward.

issues.title: PoolRefiller has no Drop impl, so pool teardown leaks the whole total_connections count
issues.verdictReason: run() bare-returns at connection_pool.rs:697 when the use-keyspace channel closes, and there is no `impl Drop for PoolRefiller` anywhere (only connection.rs:217 OrphanhoodNotifier has a Drop). conns and excess_connections are dropped with no decrement. The new test at connection_pool.rs:2011 asserts get_total_connections() == 1 after `worker.await`, i.e. after the refiller has been dropped with one connection still in it, so it encodes the leak as expected behavior.
issues.scopeReason: The teardown path and its missing decrement are unchanged from main; the PR neither introduced nor worsened it, though its new test now bakes the behaviour in.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: The PR adds metric decrements at three clear sites but there is no impl Drop for PoolRefiller and no decrement when the refiller task exits (run() returning on keyspace-channel-closed), so dropping a pool (node removal or session shutdown) leaks the full total_connections count.
reportedAs.builtin-code-review: Tearing a pool down (node removed, session dropped) leaks the count of every connection still in conns/excess_connections; this is the same accounting class the PR is closing but is pre-existing/out of scope and not covered by the new tests.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: Tearing a pool down leaks its whole count because there's no Drop on PoolRefiller; this is pre-existing and a test actually depends on this behavior.
reportedAs.tob-rust-review: When the keyspace-request channel closes and run() returns, PoolRefiller and all its Arc<Connection> entries are dropped with no decrement and no Drop impl, permanently inflating the gauge by the pool's size on every node removal or session drop.
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: Refiller teardown still leaks (the fourth discard site not fixed by the metrics-balancing commit), which the new test at line 2011 actually encodes.

issues.title: Keyspace-setup failure log downgraded from warn! to debug! as it became consequential
issues.verdictReason: The diff removes the warn!("[{}] Failed to set keyspace for new connection") from start_setting_keyspace_for_connection and re-emits the same message at debug! in the new Keyspace arm (connection_pool.rs:902-906). update_shared_conns is only reached when `!self.is_filling() && self.is_empty()`, so with any surviving connection a persistently failing USE produces nothing at default log level while the pool silently stops growing.
issues.scopeReason: The PR performed the downgrade in the same commit that made the failure fatal to the connection.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: The removed code logged the keyspace-setting failure at warn!, but the new branch logs the same message at debug!, even though the consequence is now more severe (connection dropped, pool may go Broken).
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: The spec said the pool logs the error but still reports success; the warn! at this site was replaced with debug!, so operators lose the only signal at default log level.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: Old code warned while keeping the connection; new code debugs while discarding it, and with a non-empty pool update_shared_conns isn't called, so nothing surfaces the error at default levels and the pool silently stops growing.

issues.title: Hoisting the keyspace check above maybe_reshard defers sharder and shard-aware-port discovery
issues.verdictReason: The diff moves the current_keyspace check (connection_pool.rs:911-926) above the sharding block that was previously first, so self.sharder and self.shard_aware_port are only adopted after a successful USE. keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state asserts exactly this with `assert!(refiller.sharder.is_none())` after the failed USE, so it is deliberate - but while USE keeps failing the refiller never learns the node is sharded and the PR description does not mention the change.
issues.scopeReason: The reordering is part of this diff and its documented rationale is missing from the PR description.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: Moving the keyspace check above maybe_reshard/shard-aware-port update means a connection whose USE fails never contributes its ShardInfo, so the pool never learns sharder or shard_aware_port while keyspace setup keeps failing.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: Not requested by the spec: sharder and shard-aware port are no longer adopted from a connection until USE succeeds, so a resharded node's new sharder is never learned if its keyspace is unusable, and block_advanced_shard_awareness detection is deferred behind a USE round trip; defensible but needs stating in the description.
reportedAs.tob-rust-review: Hoisting the keyspace check above the sharding block means self.sharder and self.shard_aware_port are no longer updated until USE succeeds, so while USE keeps failing the refiller never learns the node is sharded and keeps dialing the non-shard-aware port; the PR's own test suggests this is intended but the PR description doesn't mention this delay.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: Sharder adoption, maybe_reshard, and shard-aware-port discovery now run only after a successful USE, so while USE keeps failing the refiller keeps a stale sharder and stale shard-aware port.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: The reorder at :874-893 drops sharder / shard-aware-port learning on the USE-failure path; a test asserts this so it reads intentional, but it needs a one-line comment at the early return.

issues.title: decrement_total_connections does N fetch_sub(1) calls instead of one bulk Metrics helper
issues.verdictReason: connection_pool.rs:1360-1364 loops `self.metrics.dec_total_connections()`, which is a relaxed fetch_sub(1) on an AtomicU64 (metrics.rs:341-343). For PerShard pools excess_connection_limit() is 10 * nr_shards, so clearing on a 64-shard node is ~640 atomic RMWs, and a concurrent get_total_connections() can observe an intermediate value. A dec_total_connections_by(n) on Metrics/metrics_noop would be one operation and would also remove the feature-envy helper from PoolRefiller.
issues.scopeReason: The helper is added by this diff.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: for _ in 0..count { self.metrics.dec_total_connections(); } performs count separate atomic operations where a dec_total_connections_by(n) method would be one operation and read better at all three call sites.
reportedAs.builtin-code-review: Since excess_connection_limit() is 10 * nr_shards, clearing the excess pool on a 64-shard node costs ~640 atomic RMWs where a single fetch_sub(count) would do; needs a bulk helper on Metrics/metrics_noop.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: The helper issues one relaxed fetch_sub(1) per connection where a single fetch_sub(count) would suffice; only observable effect is a transient intermediate value on a relaxed counter.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: decrement_total_connections touches none of PoolRefiller's own data and is just a loop around another object's counter; it should be a Metrics method dec_total_connections_by(count) next to dec_total_connections.
reportedAs.tob-rust-review: dec_total_connections() is called in a for loop over count instead of one fetch_sub(count) call; correct but does N atomic RMWs where one would suffice.

issues.title: dec_total_connections wraps rather than saturating, so a future off-by-one underflows the gauge
issues.verdictReason: metrics.rs:341-343 is a bare `fetch_sub(1, ORDER_TYPE)` on an AtomicU64 with no saturation. The code is as described; no underflowing path is reachable today (every connection in conns/excess_connections was inc'd by count_in_metrics), so this is hardening against the four new decrement sites, two of which decrement by a computed count.
issues.scopeReason: The unsaturated fetch_sub predates the diff and no over-decrement path exists today.

reportedAs.ce-code-review: Metrics::dec_total_connections is a wrapping AtomicU64 fetch_sub with no saturation; this PR adds four new decrement sites, two by a computed count, so a future off-by-one would underflow the gauge to ~1.8e19 instead of clamping at 0.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: decrement_total_connections loops N fetch_sub(1) calls against a raw AtomicU64 fetch_sub with no saturation, so one over-decrement wraps to ~1.8e19; a saturating sub_total_connections(n) would fail safe.

issues.title: 'decrement then clear excess' pattern duplicated across three call sites, one of them drifted
issues.verdictReason: The pairing appears at connection_pool.rs:674-678 (run loop), :1031-1032 (excess limit) and :1113-1122 (maybe_reshard); the third folds in active_connection_count() and clears self.conns in between, so it is not the same shape. Two of the three sites omitted the decrement before this PR, which is exactly the failure mode a single clear_excess_connections helper would prevent.
issues.scopeReason: The duplication is created by this diff's decrement additions.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: Three independent sites must remember to pair the metric decrement with clearing excess connections; a single clear_excess_connections helper would make a fourth site impossible to get wrong, especially since two sites previously omitted the decrement before this PR.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: The pattern decrement_total_connections(excess.len()); excess_connections.clear(); appears three times at :674-677, :1031-1032, :1114-1122, and the third variant silently differs (folds in active_connection_count(), clears conns in between); should be extracted into one clear_excess_connections method.

issues.title: Private ConnectionSetupError overlaps the public ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError added in the same PR
issues.verdictReason: connection_pool.rs:1418-1421 defines `enum ConnectionSetupError { Connection(ConnectionError), Keyspace(UseKeyspaceError) }` while errors.rs:599-602 adds `ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError(#[from] UseKeyspaceError)` in the same diff, so the same two-case split is now expressible in one type. Collapsing it would lose the exhaustive local match (ConnectionError is #[non_exhaustive]), so this is a trade-off rather than a clear win.
issues.scopeReason: Both types are introduced by this diff.

reportedAs.ce-code-review: The new private ConnectionSetupError enum overlaps the public ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError variant added by the same PR; a nested match arm could carry both cases and the private enum could be deleted.

issues.title: ConnectionSetupError is undocumented and name-collides with the public ConnectionSetupRequestError
issues.verdictReason: The new enum at connection_pool.rs:1418 has no doc comment, does not implement std::error::Error, and sits in a file that imports errors::ConnectionSetupRequestError - which it also wraps transitively via ConnectionError. It is really an outcome tag for OpenedConnectionEvent, so a name like OpenedConnectionError would read more honestly.
issues.scopeReason: The type is added by this diff.

reportedAs.mattpocock-review: ConnectionSetupError sits one import away from the public ConnectionSetupRequestError and isn't an Error impl at all, just a two-way outcome tag for OpenedConnectionEvent; OpenedConnectionError would read more honestly.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: ConnectionSetupError is undocumented and name-collides with the public errors::ConnectionSetupRequestError, which it also contains.

issues.title: UseKeyspaceError under ConnectionError contradicts that type's 'connection must be dropped' doc contract
issues.verdictReason: errors.rs:570-572 documents ConnectionError as indicating 'connection can no longer be used and should be dropped', but UseKeyspaceError::KeyspaceNameMismatch and ::RequestTimeout (errors.rs:192-208) do not mean the transport is broken. Since the pool feeds this into MaybePoolConnections::Broken(ConnectionError), users see a healthy-transport failure reported as a connection-level one. The pool does drop the connection, so the contract is honoured in practice - the mismatch is in what the public type communicates.
issues.scopeReason: The variant is added by this diff.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: ConnectionError's doc comment says it indicates the connection can no longer be used and should be dropped, but UseKeyspaceError::KeyspaceNameMismatch and RequestTimeout don't mean the transport is broken; flowing into ConnectionPoolError::Broken{last_connection_error} makes users see a healthy-connection error reported as a connection-level failure.

issues.title: Two new keyspace tests omit setup_tracing(), which CONTRIBUTING.md requires
issues.verdictReason: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill (connection_pool.rs:1474) and keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state (:1526) have no setup_tracing() call, while every other test in the module does (lines 1728, 1781, 1869, 1945, 1973, 2047, 2082). CONTRIBUTING.md:84-92 ('Tracing in tests') states that any new tests should call it.

reportedAs.mattpocock-review: Two new tests at :1474 and :1526 don't call setup_tracing(), violating CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Tracing in tests' rule that any new tests should call it too; every other test in the module including three metrics tests added on this branch does.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: The two keyspace tests at :1474 and :1526 skip setup_tracing(), unlike every other test in the module.
reportedAs.tob-rust-review: The two new tests (at :1474 and :1526) don't call setup_tracing() like every other test in the module, so their tracing output is lost on failure.
reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: this is the only test in the module (along with keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill) that omits setup_tracing(), so its failures produce no log output.

issues.title: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill asserts need_filling(), which was already true before the event
issues.verdictReason: need_filling() is `!is_filling() && !is_full()` (connection_pool.rs:760-762) and on the freshly constructed refiller ready_connections is empty and the pool is empty, so the assertion holds before handle_ready_connection is called. The refiller is never run(), so nothing verifies a refill is actually scheduled; the test's other assertions (had_error_since_last_refill, Broken shared_conns, metric 0, pool_updated) are meaningful, but the name overstates what is covered.
issues.scopeReason: The test is added by this diff.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: The refiller is never run(); the test only asserts need_filling() on a static struct, verifying the predicate rather than that a refill is actually scheduled, so the test name overstates coverage.

issues.title: Hand-forged SET_KEYSPACE frame bytes in test are undocumented and can silently desync from the parser
issues.verdictReason: connection_pool.rs:1534 is `Bytes::from_static(b"\0\0\0\x03\0\x08keyspace")` with no comment explaining the layout (result kind 3 = SetKeyspace, [short] length 8, name). It is currently consistent with the RESULT parser - keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state passes - but a change to RESULT frame parsing would desync the fixture with no compile-time signal.
issues.scopeReason: The fixture is added by this diff.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: Bytes::from_static(b"\0\0\0\x03\0\x08keyspace") is a hand-encoded Result/SetKeyspace body with no comment explaining the layout (result kind 3, short length 8, name), forcing anyone changing the keyspace name to rediscover the encoding.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: The test's hand-forged SET_KEYSPACE result frame was cross-checked against Connection::verify_use_keyspace_result and is currently consistent, but a future change to RESULT frame parsing would silently desync the fixture from the production wire format with no compile-time signal.

issues.title: make_rules re-implements start_simulated_node's OPTIONS/STARTUP rules instead of parameterizing it
issues.verdictReason: The closure at connection_pool.rs:1527-1566 rebuilds the same OPTIONS->SUPPORTED and STARTUP->READY rules that start_simulated_node already constructs (connection_pool.rs:1809-1845). The duplication is not free to remove - start_simulated_node takes a non-optional ShardInfo and always advertises SIMULATED_SHARD_AWARE_PORT, while make_rules needs Option<ShardInfo>, no shard-aware port, and a QUERY rule - so parameterizing the existing helper is the suggested cleanup rather than a drop-in reuse.
issues.scopeReason: The duplicated helper is added by this diff.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: make_rules re-implements the OPTIONS/STARTUP rules that start_simulated_node already builds.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: make_rules at :1527-1566 re-implements start_simulated_node's OPTIONS/STARTUP rules instead of parameterizing the existing function.

The value cannot affect the run and misleads a reader into thinking the first connection reports sharding.
issues.scopeReason: The test is added by this diff.

issues.title: full_pool metrics test still wall-clock busy-polls despite the 'avoid busy-waiting' commit

The reviewers' suggested alternative of using pool_updated_notify is not directly available: mock_pool_refiller (connection_pool.rs:1754-1774) constructs both Notify handles inline and does not return them, so wiring an observable signal needs a helper change too.

reportedAs.superpowers-review: The avoid-busy-waiting fix at :1993-2000 is still a 1ms poll loop, and leans on select! picking the initial scheduled_refill branch with zero opens.

issues.title: maybe_reshard's excess_connections decrement term is never exercised with a non-empty excess pool
issues.verdictReason: resharding_discards_old_connections_and_balances_metrics feeds exactly one connection before resharding and then asserts excess_connections.is_empty(), so the `+ self.excess_connections.len()` half of the sum at connection_pool.rs:1113-1115 is always zero in the test; a miscount there would pass undetected.
issues.scopeReason: Both the decrement and its test are added by this diff.

reportedAs.ce-code-review: The test reshards with an empty excess_connections, so a miscount in the excess half of the new decrement sum would pass undetected.

issues.title: No test covers a pool going Broken(UseKeyspaceError) and recovering to Ready
issues.verdictReason: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state deliberately keeps one connection alive throughout, so shared_conns never becomes Broken there; keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill reaches Broken but never drives a subsequent successful USE. The Broken -> Ready transition, and with it the emit_events Lost -> Established sequence (connection_pool.rs:1158-1190), is untested.
issues.scopeReason: The Broken(UseKeyspaceError) state is newly reachable because of this diff.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: No test covers that a pool which went Broken(UseKeyspaceError) flips back to Ready once a later refill's USE succeeds.

issues.title: No test covers keyspace failure emptying the pool and firing ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost
issues.verdictReason: update_shared_conns calls emit_events (connection_pool.rs:1152-1190), which produces ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost when the pool transitions to empty. keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state keeps one connection alive so the transition never happens, and keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill constructs the refiller without a host_id, so no Lost event is produced or observed anywhere.
issues.scopeReason: This diff is what makes a keyspace failure able to empty a pool and publish Lost.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: No test covers the keyspace-failure-empties-the-pool path leading to emit_events firing a Lost connectivity event; the existing test deliberately keeps one connection alive so this path is never exercised.

issues.title: No test confirms refill backoff grows across repeated keyspace failures, or covers a USE that never answers
issues.verdictReason: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill checks only that had_error_since_last_refill is set after a single forged failure; nothing drives multiple refill cycles to observe refill_delay_strategy.on_fill_error(), and the tests forge an already-returned keyspace error rather than a USE that never responds, which is the scenario behind I3.
issues.scopeReason: Both behaviours belong to the failure path this diff introduces.

reportedAs.ce-code-review: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill checks only that the flag is set after a single failure; no test confirms refill_delay_strategy.on_fill_error() actually increases backoff across repeated failures. Existing tests forge an already-returned keyspace error rather than exercising the scenario where USE never responds.

issues.title: No test drives the increment half of the total_connections invariant end to end
issues.verdictReason: All three new metrics tests call metrics.inc_total_connections() by hand before handing an event to handle_ready_connection, rather than letting start_opening_connection's count_in_metrics closure (connection_pool.rs:1046-1053) do it, so the two halves of the invariant are never exercised together.
issues.scopeReason: The tests establishing the invariant are added by this diff, though the manual-increment pattern was inherited from existing helpers.

reportedAs.ce-code-review: The two halves of the total_connections invariant are never exercised end-to-end, mirroring an existing pattern from prior commits rather than being introduced here.

issues.title: PR description covers only one of four commits, omitting all the total_connections metric-balancing work
issues.verdictReason: The PR body describes only the keyspace-discard change (commit 7f48315d) and its Validation section lists only keyspace_setup_failure tests; commits de164845, 0d91aa54 and 617139df add decrement_total_connections, three decrement sites and three metrics tests (+415 lines) that are never mentioned, so a reader of the description alone would treat them as unexplained drive-by edits.
issues.scopeReason: The description is part of this PR and does not cover three of its four commits.

reportedAs.ce-code-review: The reviewed range contains four commits; two implement and test total_connections metric balancing on pool clears, but the PR description covers only the other two (keyspace-setup-failure discard).

issues.title: Keyspace arm sets had_error_since_last_refill even for shard-aware attempts, unlike the Connection arm

In the Keyspace arm the connection was established successfully and only USE failed, so the shard-aware port is demonstrably fine and the error is a genuine fill failure; setting the flag is the correct behaviour, not an unintended divergence.
issues.scopeReason: The arm is added by this diff.

reportedAs.mattpocock-review: The Connection arm does an immediate non-shard-aware retry and deliberately doesn't set had_error_since_last_refill for shard-aware failures, but the Keyspace arm has neither carve-out, so a keyspace failure on a shard-aware attempt inflates reconnect backoff for a reason unrelated to connectivity.

issues.title: Double-decrement of total_connections between the new bulk-clear sites and remove_connection
issues.verdictReason: remove_connection's maybe_remove_in_vec (connection_pool.rs:1224-1237) locates the connection by Arc::ptr_eq against self.conns[shard_id] and self.excess_connections. After a bulk clear the Arc is no longer in either vector, so the scan misses, the function falls through to the 'was already removed' trace, and no second decrement happens - even in the window where a stale shared_conns clone keeps the Arc alive so wait_for_error's Weak::upgrade succeeds.
